adverse_original_spans.producer_reason: EO:12823 section 1(f) replaces the original five-member government composition with a six-member composition and adds Agriculture. The complete original composition as such first ceases in 1992, although the original five agency designations are carried into the amended larger Board. EO:13131 section 1(f) later adds two more government members; neither later expansion can be the first end of the original five-member composition. The complete EO:12823 says is amended in the present tense, is dated December 3, 1992 and has no postponed effective date; later Federal Register publication does not defer these internal-government changes. EO:13131's present amendments take effect July 22, 1999; its complete text states no postponed date. Full EO:13118 is tested rather than accepted as an end: its general EO:12163 delegation expressly excludes functions otherwise delegated under EO:12757 and is subject to that order. Its separate Council membership changes do not revoke this original command. Its April 1, 1999 effectiveness, with specified October 1 exceptions, changes no first-end finding here.

rationale: Full EO 12823 cures the old missing-source gap, and the Agriculture observer deletion is correctly distinguished from retained Commerce/other permissions. Nevertheless two original scopes still combine ended numeric-composition rules with continuing substantive mandates. Original section 4(a) requires representatives from the five named agencies; EO 12823 section 1(f) changes five to six and adds Agriculture while retaining every original agency designation. Original section 4(d) directs presidential choice of private members; EO 12823 section 1(k) changes only four to five, retaining that presidential selection mandate, and EO 13131 retains presidential appointment when enlarging/recasting the provision. The producer expressly acknowledges these retained components yet assigns each entire original source span its first end in 1992. Neither continuing component has its own clause state through 2004. Changing the count does not establish termination of all operative effect in those mixed scopes. Separate or otherwise faithfully account for the continuing original mandates and the ended numerical rules, with source-governed context, before accepting a complete clause-by-clause earliest-ending claim. Whole-order end July 8, 2004 can remain supported; no automatic date change is requested.
